subject: Post-call: PayGrid model-fit eval — recommended models & next steps
messages:
From: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
To: Claire Simmons <claire@paygrid.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: PayGrid model-fit eval — recommended models & next steps

Hi Claire / Mike —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned: 

Recap
- Goal: validate whether an open-model-based serving approach can meet PayGrid's production quality bar vs your proprietary baseline (Prod-Baseline-v1) for transaction classification and intent extraction.
- Success criteria you mentioned: >= 95% intent-labeling agreement with your annotated set and human-acceptance >= 85% on edge cases.

Redwood recommended starting models (prioritized):
1) Llama-3 13B (quantized, 8-bit) — best balance latency/cost with strong instruction-following.
2) Mistral-Instruct-7B — good on concise instruction tasks and cheaper throughput.
3) RedWood-Opt-Chat-7B (our curated finetune + quant profile) — tuned for customer-like transaction semantics.

Why these? In our internal benchmarks they consistently reach parity within ~3-5% of retail-size proprietary baselines on semantic-similarity metrics and achieve high human-accept rates when prompt engineering for label consistency. We’ll provide the detailed comparatives below.

Attached: evaluation_prompt_set_v2.csv (10k sample prompts derived from your seed set) and a short model_comparison_20260810.pdf with metric-level summaries.

Proposed evaluation plan (2-week rapid cycle):
- Day 0–2: we exchange a 10k labeled sample + access details (S3 or secure upload).
- Day 3–7: Redwood runs automated batch evals (ROUGE, semantic-sim, F1 on slot extraction) + cost/latency measurements.
- Day 8–12: human review on edge-case buckets (100–200 examples).
- Day 13–14: joint review + acceptance decision.

Acceptance thresholds (suggested):
- Intent agreement: >= 95% (exact-match or 0.9+ semantic-similarity threshold)
- Slot extraction F1: within 5% of Prod-Baseline-v1
- Human acceptance on edge cases: >= 85%

Risks & mitigation:
- Quality regressions during quantization: we’ll run full-precision checks and fall back to 16-bit paths for flagged examples.
- Cost/latency tradeoffs: we’ll provide profiling results per model and recommend batching/kv-cache settings for steady-state.

Next steps (action items):
- Claire: confirm which S3 bucket or secure upload you prefer and share credentials or a presigned URL.
- Mike: please confirm the three label schemas you want included in the eval (intent, amount-extraction, fraud-flag).
- Redwood (me + Marissa): we’ll kick off the eval once data is shared and schedule a 30-min check-in at Day 7.

Thanks — I’ll stand up the eval harness as soon as we get the data.

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0182

Attachments: evaluation_prompt_set_v2.csv (csv stub, 10k rows), model_comparison_20260810.pdf (summary)

Thanks Lauren — really helpful summary. A few quick clarifications: 

1) Latency & cost: for our production constraints we need 95th pctl latency < 250ms for single-turn classification and steady-state cost target below $0.0015 per request. Can Redwood profile and provide estimated costs for both the Llama-3 13B quantized and Mistral-7B options?

2) Prompt set: please send the prompt CSV (we saw the attachment but didn’t download in the call). We’ll also share a small private set of edge cases (about 200).

3) Acceptance criteria: we’re comfortable with the intent agreement threshold you proposed, but for slot extraction would you be willing to add an upper bound SLA for drift — e.g., if F1 drops >5% vs baseline we trigger a rollback?

We can do the upload to the S3 bucket paygrid-evals-us-east-1. I’ll share a presigned URL by EOD.

—Claire
Head of ML Platforms | PayGrid
claire@paygrid.com

Mistral-Instruct-7B shows ~80–120ms p95 and estimated cost ~ $0.0005–$0.0008. These are estimates; we’ll provide exact numbers after the Day 3 run.

Prompt CSV & edge cases:
- Attached evaluation_prompt_set_v2.csv — includes label columns and a column for 'edge_bucket' that we’ll use to prioritize human review. Please upload your 200-edge cases to the same S3 location and mark them with edge_bucket=paygrid-private-200.

Drift rollback SLA:
- We can include a rollback trigger for production if F1 drops >5% vs baseline during the A/B rollout. We’ll document the rollback procedure in the runbook and include an automated monitor.

Next scheduling: 
- We’ll kick off the eval once presigned URL is live. Proposed check-in: Aug 17 @ 10am PT (30 min) after the automated run. Does that work for you?

I’ll add Marissa to coordinate resource allocation for the eval.

Thanks —
Lauren
